answer: Peers stake POA on the score they assign. Spot checks re-grade one in ten and take any difference out of the reviewer's stake, so a careless panel loses capital while a careful one keeps it. Each unverified claim cuts the submitter's payout until someone checks it, which pushes answers toward claims a stranger can confirm. Auditors come from a rotating pool, so the same panel never grades one submitter twice. The cipher of a score means nothing until a second reader reproduces it, and the nectar here is verified work, which is why a lotus of clean answers takes epochs to open.
